name: Loop bound guarantees full traversal of each list vs. bound capped by the other list's size (min-length truncation)
side_a: No deduct when each list is traversed by a bound that covers its own full length (for-each over the collection, or `i < thisList.size()`), even if the two lists are visited in separate/nested loops or one is pre-indexed into a map — every element of both lists is reachable by the declared bounds.
side_b: Deduct when the declared loop bound is a conjunction/minimum tying the index to the other collection's size (e.g., `i < historyList.size() && i < mathList.size()`), so by the bounds themselves the elements beyond the shorter list's length in the longer list are never accessed. This is a bounds defect, not an 'early return' exception.

name: Tolerance of wrong comparison/equality semantics vs. requiring semantically correct use of the returned values
side_a: No_deduct when both getStudentID and getAbsences are invoked on CourseRecord elements, even if the values they return are used with flawed semantics — reference equality `==` on the String IDs, `>=` instead of `>` for the absence comparison, summing differences instead of counting students, or an early `break` that skips matches. Credit tracks whether the two accessors were called on list elements, not whether the surrounding logic computes the right answer.
side_b: Deduct whenever the values returned by getStudentID/getAbsences are used incorrectly (e.g., comparing IDs with `==`, using `>=` where `>` is required, returning a sum rather than a count), on the view that an accessor used in a semantically wrong comparison does not count as a correct call.

name: Records paired by looked-up student ID vs. assumed index-aligned lists with no ID lookup
side_a: No_deduct when the response actually retrieves student IDs from list elements to pair a history record with a math record (nested loop, map keyed on getStudentID, etc.), so getStudentID is genuinely exercised on a CourseRecord drawn from historyList/mathList.
side_b: Deduct when the response pairs records by position/index (`historyList.get(i)` with `mathList.get(i)`) and therefore never retrieves a student ID at all — the matching step that requires getStudentID is skipped entirely, so only getAbsences is ever called.

name: strict `>` comparison vs. non-strict `>=` comparison of absences
side_a: no_deduct if the comparison that drives the counting uses the strict greater-than operator (`>`) between a history absence value and a math absence value — the comparison then actually tests 'more absences than', which is what the item asks for.
side_b: deduct if the comparison uses a non-strict operator such as `>=` (or `<=`, `==`) instead of a strict `>`, even when the operands, direction, and surrounding control flow are otherwise correct; `historyAbs >= mathAbs` is true for equal absence counts and therefore does not identify that one element has MORE absences than the other.

name: Correctness of the guarding test (comparison operator, ID-matching method, loop pairing): irrelevant vs must be logically correct
side_a: Do not deduct for logical errors in how the two records are paired or compared, so long as some conditional inside a loop guards the increment. Credit `>=` instead of `>`, `==` instead of `.equals()` for String IDs, a HashMap lookup instead of a nested loop, or even a parallel-index assumption that never matches IDs — this sub-item only asks that a counter be incremented within a conditional inside a loop.
side_b: Deduct unless the conditional actually tests the correct thing: IDs compared with `.equals()` across both lists (or an equivalent correct lookup) and history absences strictly greater than math absences. Deduct for `>=`, for reference comparison of IDs, or for pairing records by index rather than by student.

name: What is accumulated: any numeric accumulation vs exactly one unit per qualifying student
side_a: Do not deduct when the variable accumulates a non-unit quantity (e.g., the difference in absences) rather than a per-student tally; adding any value to the accumulator inside the conditional satisfies 'increments it within a conditional statement'.
side_b: Deduct unless the accumulator is advanced by exactly one per qualifying student, so that it represents a count of students rather than a sum of some other quantity.

name: Pairs records by actual student-ID matching (.equals / map keyed by ID) vs by reference-== or by list position
side_a: No deduct if the two courses' records are paired by comparing student IDs by value — either `String.equals(...)` or a lookup structure keyed on `getStudentID()`.
side_b: Deduct if records are paired by `==` on the ID Strings (reference comparison) or by parallel index/position in the two lists, so the same student is not reliably identified.

name: Returns a count of qualifying students vs returns an accumulated absence-difference total
side_a: No deduct if the returned value is an incremented counter of students satisfying the comparison (`count++`).
side_b: Deduct if the returned value is a sum/aggregate of absence differences rather than a count of students.
